21.description: Saskatoon will fund $8,500 for a public art mentorship program in 2026. It will pair emerging artists with experienced mentors to build skills and diversify the talent pool for future public art projects.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Mentors and mentees will receive honorariums aligned with CARFAC rates.
Program will focus on diversity in selecting mentors and mentees.

24.description: The committee recommends a new Development Incentives Policy to boost affordable housing and strategic redevelopment in Saskatoon's city center, growth corridors, and some established neighborhoods.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
4 for, 2 against
Developers face high costs for land assembly and infill projects in older areas.
Administration recommended targeted incentives
The new policy replaces the Innovative Housing and Vacant Lot Incentive Programs.
Mayor Block asked if other cities have secondary corridor plans, which was not answered.
Councillor Parker expressed concern about not understanding the consequences of changing the policy.
The policy prioritizes affordable housing with full site tax abatements for 15% affordable units.

18.description: Saskatoon will provide $13,517.50 in heritage conservation funding for exterior painting and wood pillar repairs at the Larkin House, located at 925 5th Avenue North.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Owners of Larkin House at 925 5th Avenue North receive funding for repairs.

20.description: The committee recommends applying for up to $1.5 million in federal funding for the Riversdale Streetscaping Project to plant 125 trees and related infrastructure.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Riversdale residents will benefit from 125 new trees and streetscaping.
Project will plant 125 trees, expanding the community tree canopy.

26.description: The committee recommends increasing the golf course driving range project budget by $1.615 million to $3.015 million, funded by the Golf Course Capital Reserve, for new netting at Holiday Park and Silverwood golf courses.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Golfers at Holiday Park and Silverwood courses.
Administration plans pole installation this fall, netting by spring 2027.

25.description: Saskatoon will explore expanding higher-density housing policies to major streets beyond current transit corridors, potentially increasing housing options city-wide.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Administration flagged a risk of diluting growth focus from main transit corridors.
The decision establishes a new 'secondary plan approach' for growth beyond transit corridors.
Administration will report back with details on implementing the secondary plan approach.

22.description: Saskatoon is reviewing its Neighborhood Services Program, which supports 47 community associations, to address changing demographics, declining volunteer capacity, and rising costs, ensuring it meets current community needs.

chips.text: Over 500 volunteers deliver programs and events for community associations.
Administration will present future reports outlining program changes and resource implications.

23.description: Saskatoon's Community Services Division issued 404,289 building permits, created 4,661 new residential units, and saved 300,000 cubic meters of water in 2025.

chips.text: Councillor Jeffries asked how to share division successes with the community.
New residential units created for 4,661 households.
College Quarter Plan was the first approved through the Quarter Planning Program.
Evapotranspiration technology saved 300,000 cubic meters of water in parks.
Administration will work with communications to share division stories on the website.

27.description: Council reviews a list of reports requested by the Planning, Development and Community Services Committee, with administration providing timelines for their completion.

28.description: Council referred a petition to administration for a report on repealing the heritage designation for St. Mark's Church at 1406 8th Avenue North.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
The Anglican Diocese of Saskatoon owns the former St. Mark's Church property.
Bishop McCharles requested repealing the heritage designation for the church property.
